page.layout: One page of running text in a single column; no marginal notes. Running head at top, page number 172; catchword "Dispu-" at the lower right.

main_text.p: usui esse possunt, nō satis consideremus, nec etiam recte æstimemus? Atqui non solum quid mali, sed etiam quid boni rebus nostris insit, spectandum erat: & mala quidem corrigenda pro virili, bona aut agnoscenda erant, & eorum auctor Deus celebrandus.

i. Lucet, inæstimabili Dei dono, Euangelij lux, quam Sol iustitiæ Iesvs Christvs, Antichristianis tenebris pulsis & dissipatis, his postremis temporibus, accedit. Nec post tempora Augustini, Hieronymi, Ambrosij & aliorum, qui [illegible, ~8 letters] fuerūt, tanta fuit perspicuitate tradita Ecclesię doctrina in floretissimis & cultissimis ciuitatibus & provincijs, quanta nunc traditur etiā in obscuris quibusdā pagis.

2. Diuinitus etiam excitati & illustrati sunt quidam lucidissimi φωστῆρες & docto res Ecclesiæ, qui docendo, Scripturas diuinas interpretando, & cum hostibus veritatis differendo, plantant & rigant ar-vum Dei, incremento largiente Domino.
Quis etiam non videat, triarijs regni Pō-tificij, & inter alios Turriano, illustrem ἀνταγωνιστήν[?] oppositum à Domino exercituum, qui unus multorum instar est, ac Dispu-

page.notes: Head line "172 HYPOMNEMATA" read as printed; long s normalised to s, u/v and i/j normalised. Small-caps "Iesvs Christvs" transcribed in roman letters. Greek word after "qui" is too faint to read; marked illegible. "ἀνταγωνιστήν" is a best reading, marked [?]. The numerals "i." and "2." are old-style forms and were given as 1 and 2 in the text. "Pō-" is printed with a macron over the o (Pon-tificij), kept as printed. "Dispu-" is the catchword at the foot.
